_meta.description: Unified source manifest — definitive reference for all dietology data sources. Merges base sources.json with overlay-specific metadata from sources-overlay.json and dataset catalog from data-index.json.
_meta.relationship: This file is the SINGLE authoritative source reference. sources.json and sources-overlay.json are intermediate inputs — model should load ONLY this file.

description: Source manifest for the dietology knowledge base. Every data file references a source_id from this manifest via its _meta block. The model loads this file first. THIS IS THE DEFINITIVE VERSION — supersedes sources.json. to understand what data is available and the reliability tier of each source.

usda-fdc-2026-04.name: USDA FoodData Central
usda-fdc-2026-04.description: Nutrient composition of 7800+ foods per 100g. Macronutrients, micronutrients, amino acid profiles, fatty acids. US government authoritative source.

who-gho.name: WHO Global Health Observatory — Epidemiological Indicators
who-gho.format: OData JSON API dump. Parser: extract-who-gho.py
who-gho.description: Epidemiological statistics: anaemia prevalence in non-pregnant women (242 countries, 1995–2019), overweight/BMI≥25 prevalence (210 countries, 1990–2022), diabetes prevalence age-standardized (210 countries, 1990–2022). All values are modelled estimates with 95% CI — not raw survey data. Statistical modelling ensures cross-country comparability.

msd-manual-dri.name: MSD Manual Professional — DRI Tables
msd-manual-dri.license: Copyright Merck & Co. — numeric facts not copyrightable
msd-manual-dri.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI values are facts, not creative expression. Attribution: 'Based on National Academies DRI, as reproduced in MSD Manual Professional Edition.'
msd-manual-dri.authority_note: Reproduces National Academies DRI values in HTML format. Peer-reviewed professional medical reference published since 1899.
msd-manual-dri.description: Dietary Reference Intakes (RDA, AI, UL) for 11 vitamins and 9 trace minerals by age and sex. Values extracted via HTML parser, metadata (ul_note, unit_note, proper unit names) from manual transcription.
msd-manual-dri.tier_note: Upgraded from B: all values and metadata now machine-verified via extract-msd-dri-parser.py. 0 manual transcription dependencies.

msd-macronutrients-per-kg.name: MSD Manual — Macronutrients DRI per kg
msd-macronutrients-per-kg.license: Copyright Merck & Co. — numeric facts not copyrightable
msd-macronutrients-per-kg.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI values are facts. Source: Institute of Medicine. Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium, Phosphorus, Magnesium, Vitamin D, and Fluoride. Washington, DC: National Academy Press; 1997.
msd-macronutrients-per-kg.format: HTML table (structured, parseable). All values in mg/kg of body weight.
msd-macronutrients-per-kg.authority_note: Reproduces IOM 1997 per-kg values. These are the PRIMARY form — absolute DRI values are derived by multiplying by reference body weights. Per-kg values are MORE accurate for individual use: multiply by actual body weight, not population reference weight.
msd-macronutrients-per-kg.description: Calcium, Phosphorus, Magnesium DRI in mg/kg for 17 age/sex groups. All values in mg/kg — model MUST multiply by individual body weight. Infants: AI. Children and adults: RDA.
msd-macronutrients-per-kg.tier_note: Upgraded from B: values now machine-verified via extract-msd-dri-parser.py. Per-kg values are the primary form from IOM 1997 — more accurate for individual use than absolute DRI.
msd-macronutrients-per-kg.convention: All values in mg/kg of body weight. Multiply by individual body weight for absolute daily intake. More accurate for individual use than fixed absolute DRI values.

msd-consumer-minerals.name: MSD Manual Consumer — Overview of Minerals
msd-consumer-minerals.license: Copyright Merck & Co. — numeric facts not copyrightable
msd-consumer-minerals.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI values are facts, not creative expression. Adult RDA/AI values only — no pediatric or adolescent age breakdown.
msd-consumer-minerals.authority_note: Consumer edition of MSD Manual. Adult RDA/AI values only. Values superseded by nas-dri-2019 (Na/K: 22 groups, machine-verified). Retained as metadata source only.
msd-consumer-minerals.description: Adult RDA/AI for Na and K — metadata source only. Values in overlay now come from NAS 2019 (22 groups, machine-verified).
msd-consumer-minerals.tier_note: Tier B because adult values only. Now superseded by nas-dri-2019 for Na/K — retained for metadata (notes, per-group annotations) only.
msd-consumer-minerals.limitation: Metadata only. Na/K values now from NAS 2019 (22 groups). Retained for per-group notes and nutrient-level metadata.

iom-dri-1997.name: IOM Dietary Reference Intakes — Ca, P, Mg, Vitamin D, Fluoride (1997)
iom-dri-1997.license: Free PDF download — numeric facts not copyrightable
iom-dri-1997.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI values are facts established by the US/Canadian governments. Full citation: Institute of Medicine. 1997. Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium, Phosphorus, Magnesium, Vitamin D, and Fluoride. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press.
iom-dri-1997.format: PDF with text layer (born-digital, 1997). Cross-verified via NCBI Bookshelf machine-readable HTML.
iom-dri-1997.authority_note: Original DRI report establishing RDA/AI for P and Mg. Values extracted from NCBI Bookshelf HTML rendering (clean machine-parseable table, same IOM 1997 source) and cross-verified against manual transcription: 24/28 groups 100% match, 4 PARTIAL_MATCH due to pregnancy/breastfeeding granularity difference (teen vs adult). UL values from LPI (lpi-mic-minerals) — IOM 1997 PDF scrambled, LPI HTML provides clean machine-readable reproduction.
iom-dri-1997.description: Current DRI for phosphorus and magnesium. RDA/AI values from NCBI Bookshelf (ttt00057_1 table) — machine-readable rendering of IOM 1997 RDA/AI summary. UL values from Linus Pauling Institute (machine-readable HTML, cites IOM 1997). Cross-verified against manual transcription from original PDF.

cross_verification_results.partial_match_note: 4 pregnancy/breastfeeding groups: manual used adult values for consolidated groups, NCBI shows per-subgroup values. Teen values (≤18y) are systematically higher. Overlay uses NCBI per-subgroup values for finest granularity.

ncbi-iom1997-summary.name: NCBI Bookshelf — IOM 1997 DRI Summary Tables
ncbi-iom1997-summary.license: Numeric facts not copyrightable — HTML rendering of public government report
ncbi-iom1997-summary.mit_compatible_note: Machine-readable HTML version of IOM 1997 DRI summary tables. Same Tier A source as IOM 1997 PDF. Numeric DRI values are facts established by the US/Canadian governments. Full citation: Institute of Medicine. 1997. Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium, Phosphorus, Magnesium, Vitamin D, and Fluoride. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press.
ncbi-iom1997-summary.format: HTML table via NCBI Bookshelf ?report=objectonly endpoint (structured, machine-parseable).
ncbi-iom1997-summary.authority_note: Same IOM 1997 DRI report as the original PDF, rendered by NCBI in clean HTML. Used for automated cross-verification of P and Mg values manually transcribed from scrambled PDF. NOT an independent Tier B source — this IS the Tier A IOM 1997 in machine-readable form.
ncbi-iom1997-summary.description: Machine-readable HTML rendering of IOM 1997 DRI RDA/AI summary table. Columns: Ca, P, Mg, Vitamin D, Fluoride, Thiamin, Riboflavin, Niacin, B6, Folate, B12, Pantothenic Acid, Biotin. Used for cross-verification of manually transcribed phosphorus and magnesium values from the scrambled IOM 1997 PDF.

crosscheck_summary.partial_match_note: 4 pregnancy/breastfeeding groups show partial match because dri-minerals.json consolidates teen (≤18y) and adult subgroups into a single group using adult value. NCBI source shows per-subgroup values. Adult values match 100%; teen values differ as expected for consolidated groups.

iom-dri-2011.name: IOM Dietary Reference Intakes — Calcium and Vitamin D (2011)
iom-dri-2011.license: Free PDF download — numeric facts not copyrightable
iom-dri-2011.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI values are facts established by the US/Canadian governments. Full citation: Institute of Medicine. 2011. Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium and Vitamin D. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press.
iom-dri-2011.format: PDF with text layer (born-digital, 2011). Parser: extract-iom-dri.py (pdfplumber).
iom-dri-2011.authority_note: Current authoritative DRI for Calcium. Supersedes IOM 1997 values for this nutrient. Provides finest granularity: 22 age/sex groups including teen/adult pregnancy/breastfeeding subgroups with separate UL groups.
iom-dri-2011.description: Current DRI tables for calcium across all age/sex groups. Extracted from Table S-1 (Summary Tables, pp. 499–542). Calcium RDA/AI + UL groups per age.

nasem-dri-2006.name: National Academies DRI — The Essential Guide to Nutrient Requirements
nasem-dri-2006.license: Free PDF download — numeric facts not copyrightable
nasem-dri-2006.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI values are facts established by the US/Canadian governments. Full citation: Institute of Medicine. 2006. Dietary Reference Intakes: The Essential Guide to Nutrient Requirements. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press.
nasem-dri-2006.format: PDF with text layer (born-digital, 2006). Summary Tables: pp. 529–542
nasem-dri-2006.authority_note: Comprehensive DRI summary for all nutrients. The Food and Nutrition Board of the National Academies is the body that establishes DRI values for the United States and Canada.
nasem-dri-2006.description: Complete DRI compendium: RDA, EAR, AI, UL for all nutrients across all age/sex groups. Gold standard primary source. Extraction from PDF tables for cross-validation with MSD Manual values.
nasem-dri-2006.status: deferred — PDF download requires free account

who-2024-hb.name: WHO 2024 Guideline on Haemoglobin Cutoffs to Define Anaemia
who-2024-hb.mit_compatible_note: ⚠️ NC restriction. Numeric threshold values are facts (not copyrightable). Direct reproduction of WHO tables would violate NC clause. Extracted facts with attribution are defensible. Bundled use in MIT project — legal grey area.
who-2024-hb.format: PDF with text layer (born-digital, 2024). Structured tables.
who-2024-hb.description: Updated diagnostic thresholds for anaemia: lowered cutoff for children 6-23 months (105 g/L, previously 110), added trimester-specific pregnancy cutoffs (2nd trimester: 105 g/L). Severity classification (mild/moderate/severe). Altitude and smoking adjustments.

wikipedia-lab-ranges.name: Wikipedia — Reference Ranges for Blood Tests
wikipedia-lab-ranges.mit_compatible_note: CC BY-SA covers wiki text, not numeric facts. Attribution required. Uses data sourced from MedlinePlus (public domain), Uppsala University Hospital, Mayo Clinic, GPnotebook, First Aid for USMLE, and ~200 other cited sources.
wikipedia-lab-ranges.authority_note: Aggregates values from multiple secondary and primary sources. Reference ranges vary between laboratories and assay methods — these are representative values, not universal norms. Suitable for contextualization, not diagnostic recommendations.
wikipedia-lab-ranges.description: Most comprehensive public machine-readable compendium of laboratory reference ranges. 300+ tests covering hematology, chemistry, endocrinology, immunology, coagulation, vitamins. All values with citation tracing to primary sources.

open-food-facts.name: Open Food Facts
open-food-facts.format: JSONL daily export, Parquet (Hugging Face), CSV, REST JSON API
open-food-facts.authority_note: Crowdsourced — quality varies. Largest open food product database (3.7M+ products). Useful for barcode lookup of branded products.
open-food-facts.description: Branded food products with barcodes, ingredients, nutrition facts panels. Crowdsourced data — quality is uneven. Included as catalog expansion, not primary nutrient reference.

hl7-fhir-nutrition.name: HL7 FHIR Nutrition Resources
hl7-fhir-nutrition.format: JSON, XML, Turtle — standard schemas, not data
hl7-fhir-nutrition.authority_note: International healthcare data exchange standard. Not a data source — provides reference data models for NutritionOrder, NutritionIntake, NutritionObservation.
hl7-fhir-nutrition.description: Standard FHIR resources for nutrition data modeling. Reference for designing internal data structures, not a source of clinical knowledge.

lpi-mic-minerals.name: Linus Pauling Institute — Micronutrient Information Center (Minerals)
lpi-mic-minerals.license: Copyright Oregon State University — numeric facts not copyrightable
lpi-mic-minerals.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI UL values are facts, not creative expression. LPI reproduces IOM 1997 UL values for Phosphorus and Magnesium in machine-readable HTML tables. Attribution: 'Based on IOM DRI 1997, as reproduced by Linus Pauling Institute, Oregon State University.'
lpi-mic-minerals.authority_note: Academic peer-reviewed source that faithfully reproduces IOM DRI UL values. Not independent from IOM (cites IOM 1997), but provides clean machine-readable HTML tables. Magnesium UL applies to supplemental magnesium only, not food sources.
lpi-mic-minerals.description: Tolerable Upper Intake Levels (UL) for Phosphorus (9 age groups: infants, children 1-3/4-8/9-13yr, adolescents 14-18yr, adults 19-70yr, adults >70yr, pregnancy, breastfeeding) and Magnesium (6 age groups: infants, children 1-3/4-8/9-13yr, adolescents 14-18yr, adults 19+yr). UL for Magnesium applies to supplemental magnesium only.
lpi-mic-minerals.based_on: Institute of Medicine DRI reports (1997 for P/Mg)
lpi-mic-minerals.tier_note: Tier B — authoritative academic secondary source. Reproduces IOM 1997 UL values in clean machine-readable HTML tables where IOM PDF is scrambled.

nas-dri-2019.name: NASEM Dietary Reference Intakes — Sodium and Potassium (2019)
nas-dri-2019.license: Free PDF download — numeric facts not copyrightable
nas-dri-2019.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI values are facts established by the US/Canadian governments. Full citation: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine. 2019. Dietary Reference Intakes for Sodium and Potassium. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press.
nas-dri-2019.format: PDF with text layer (born-digital, 2019). 4-page Highlights summary. Parser: extract-nas-dri-2019.py (pdfplumber).
nas-dri-2019.authority_note: Current authoritative DRI for Sodium and Potassium in US/Canada. Supersedes IOM 2005 values. Introduces CDRR (Chronic Disease Risk Reduction Intake) concept. UL=ND for both nutrients — authoritative determination, not data gap.
nas-dri-2019.description: Current DRI for sodium and potassium: AI by age/sex/life-stage (22 groups each), CDRR for sodium. Table 1: Potassium AI. Table 2: Sodium AI + CDRR. 22 groups including infant, children, male/female (6 age brackets), pregnant (3 age brackets), breastfeeding (3 age brackets).

who-smart-guidelines.name: WHO SMART Guidelines (FHIR R4)
who-smart-guidelines.license: Code: BSD-like. Content: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
who-smart-guidelines.mit_compatible_note: Software artifacts (BSD-like) — MIT-compatible. Clinical content (CC BY-NC-SA) — NC restriction. Currently focused on ANC (pregnancy), limited adult nutrition coverage.
who-smart-guidelines.description: Machine-readable clinical decision support in FHIR format. ANC Dietary Counselling and related guidelines. Limited scope for general adult nutrition. Content under NC license restricts bundled use.

dietology-data-index.name: Dietology Data Index — Unified Manifest
dietology-data-index.authority_note: Autogenerated manifest of all knowledge base files. Not a data source — an index of sources and datasets.
dietology-data-index.description: Unified manifest of all dietology knowledge base files with domains, tiers, sources, and statistics. Generated from 6 production datasets.

lab_reference_ranges_tier_a_b.description: No authoritative machine-readable (Tier A/B) source of laboratory reference ranges exists. Primary sources (MedlinePlus, clinical guidelines) either lack numeric values on their pages or are narrative PDFs. Wikipedia (Tier C) is the only machine-readable compendium.
lab_reference_ranges_tier_a_b.impact: System can contextualize lab results ('your ferritin is 15, typical range 12-150') but cannot make authoritative diagnostic statements. Reference ranges vary by lab method and population.
lab_reference_ranges_tier_a_b.mitigation: flag lab ranges as Tier C in model context; model must qualify any range-based statement with source tier and recommend clinical verification.

micronutrient_deficiency_thresholds.description: WHO publishes deficiency thresholds for vitamin A, zinc, iodine, ferritin (iron), and other micronutrients, but only in narrative PDFs — not machine-readable. Haemoglobin is the sole exception (WHO 2024 guideline has structured, extractable tables).
micronutrient_deficiency_thresholds.impact: Anaemia screening is covered (Hb thresholds). Other micronutrient deficiency screening (vitamin A, zinc, iron stores via ferritin) lacks authoritative machine-readable diagnostic cutoffs.
micronutrient_deficiency_thresholds.mitigation: monitor WHO for structured data releases. Alternatively: extract numeric facts from WHO PDFs (defensible as facts, but borderline under machine-readable constraint — risk of extraction errors from narrative text vs structured tables).

clinical_nutrition_guidelines.description: No machine-readable clinical nutrition support guidelines exist for general adult conditions (ESPEN excluded — narrative PDF). WHO SMART Guidelines cover pregnancy only (ANC) and have NC content restrictions.
clinical_nutrition_guidelines.impact: System cannot provide evidence-based nutrition support recommendations backed by a machine-readable authoritative source for conditions like malnutrition, obesity, post-surgery nutrition, oncology nutrition.
clinical_nutrition_guidelines.mitigation: explicitly document as a system limitation. HL7 FHIR provides data models (not clinical content). Monitor WHO SMART Guidelines for adult nutrition scope expansion.

dri-minerals-overlay.json.description: 14 minerals (Ca, P, Mg, Na, K, Fe, Zn, Cu, I, Se, Mn, Cr, Mo, F), 254 groups at finest available granularity. 0 manual_transcription, 0 manual source file dependencies — all values and metadata machine-verified or programmatically generated.
input_files: data/dri-p-mg-ul-parsed.json (P/Mg UL, LPI based on IOM 1997)
dri-minerals-overlay.json.ul_machine_verified: All 14 nutrients: trace minerals (MSD Professional), Calcium (IOM 2011), Sodium/Potassium (NAS 2019), Phosphorus/Magnesium (LPI based on IOM 1997)
dri-minerals-overlay.json.pregnancy_breastfeeding_granularity: split into teen (14-18yr), adult 19-30yr, adult 31-50yr for all nutrients (Ca, P, Mg, Na, K, trace minerals)

dri-vitamins-overlay.json.description: 11 vitamins, 154 groups. All values and metadata machine-extracted from MSD HTML. 0 manual transcription.
input_files: data/dri-vitamins-parsed.json (machine-parsed values + metadata: unit, UL, ul_unit, ul_note, unit_note, 11×14=154 groups)
dri-vitamins-overlay.json.pregnancy_breastfeeding_granularity: single group (19-50yr), no teen split. MSD vitamins table does not provide teen/adult breakdown for pregnancy/breastfeeding — source limitation, not extraction error.

dri-macronutrients-per-kg-overlay.json.description: 3 nutrients (Ca/P/Mg in mg/kg), 51 groups. All values machine-parsed. Per-kg values — model must multiply by individual body weight. 0 manual transcription.
dri-macronutrients-per-kg-overlay.json.convention: All values in mg/kg of body weight. Multiply by individual body weight. Infants: AI. Children and adults: RDA.

who-anaemia-nonpregnant-prevalence.json.description: Anaemia prevalence in non-pregnant women (15–49) by country, year, and severity — 20,950 records (242 countries, 1995–2019)

who-bmi-overweight-prevalence.json.description: Prevalence of overweight (BMI ≥25) among adults 18+ by country, year, and sex — 20,790 records (210 countries, 1990–2022)

who-diabetes-prevalence.json.description: Age-standardized diabetes prevalence by country, year, sex, and age group — 41,580 records (210 countries, 1990–2022)

dri-minerals-overlay.json.description: 14 minerals, 254 groups, finest granularity per source. 0 manual_transcription.
dri-minerals-overlay.json.notes: Ca: IOM 2011 (22 groups + ul_groups). P/Mg: IOM 1997 via NCBI cross-verification (22 groups each), UL from LPI (based on IOM 1997). Trace minerals: MSD Professional (16 groups each), UL from MSD Professional. Na/K: NAS 2019 (22 groups each). Pregnancy/breastfeeding split into teen/adult subgroups. All 14 nutrients have machine-verified UL metadata.

dri-vitamins-overlay.json.description: 11 vitamins, 154 groups, machine-parsed values with full metadata
dri-vitamins-overlay.json.notes: Values and metadata (unit, UL, ul_unit, ul_note, unit_note) all machine-extracted from MSD Professional HTML. 0 manual transcription. Pregnancy/breastfeeding are single groups without age split — MSD vitamins table does not provide teen/adult breakdown.

dri-macronutrients-per-kg-overlay.json.description: 3 nutrients (Ca/P/Mg), 51 groups (17 each), mg/kg of body weight
dri-macronutrients-per-kg-overlay.json.notes: Values machine-parsed; category/note/citation programmatically generated. 0 manual transcription. Per-kg values — model must multiply by individual body weight. More accurate for individual use than absolute DRI. Infants: AI. Children and adults: RDA. Based on IOM 1997.

usda-foundation-foods-essential.json.description: 363 foods with nutrient composition (per 100g), 27 essential nutrients
usda-foundation-foods-essential.json.notes: Subset of USDA Foundation Foods (CC0). Filtered to foods with complete nutrient profiles for 27 essential nutrients.

lab-reference-ranges.json.description: 254 lab test reference ranges across 16 categories
lab-reference-ranges.json.notes: Wikipedia-sourced reference ranges. Tier C: useful for context but not authoritative clinical reference. Values are population averages, not individual diagnostic thresholds.

who-hb-thresholds.json.notes: WHO 2024 Guideline on haemoglobin cutoffs. Includes severity classification (mild/moderate/severe), altitude/smoking adjustments, pregnancy-specific thresholds.

who-anaemia-nonpregnant-prevalence.json.description: Anaemia prevalence in non-pregnant women (15–49) by country, year, and severity — 20,950 records (242 countries, 1995–2019)
who-anaemia-nonpregnant-prevalence.json.notes: WHO GHO modelled estimates. Not raw survey data — statistical modelling for cross-country comparability. Values with 95% CI. CC BY 4.0.

who-bmi-overweight-prevalence.json.description: Prevalence of overweight (BMI ≥25) among adults 18+ by country, year, and sex — 20,790 records (210 countries, 1990–2022)
who-bmi-overweight-prevalence.json.notes: WHO GHO age-standardized estimates. Both-sex (BTSX), male (MLE), female (FMLE) breakdowns. Values with 95% CI. CC BY 4.0.

who-diabetes-prevalence.json.description: Age-standardized diabetes prevalence (raised fasting glucose ≥7.0 mmol/L or on medication) by country, year, sex, and age group — 41,580 records (210 countries, 1990–2022)
who-diabetes-prevalence.json.notes: WHO GHO age-standardized estimates. Age groups: 18+ and 30+. Sex breakdowns: BTSX, MLE, FMLE. Values with 95% CI. CC BY 4.0.

sources-final.json.description: Unified source manifest — definitive reference for all dietology data sources (15 sources, 5 tier levels)
sources-final.json.notes: Merges sources.json (base) + sources-overlay.json (DRI overlay) + data-index.json (catalog). Single authoritative source reference — model loads ONLY this file. Supersedes sources.json.

build_pipeline.description: Full rebuild via unified script build-all.py. Parses source documents, builds overlays, generates index and manifest. Handles circular dependency (data-index ↔ sources-final) automatically.
